mission.display_title: Connect the Poisson process to the Poisson distribution
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to place the Poisson process beside the Poisson distribution you already recognise — so counting arrivals in continuous time connects honestly to the discrete Poisson count model, without swallowing inverse-transform generation.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to state the Poisson process story and its link to Poisson counts (and related waiting-time cues as the CMP presents) — and to refuse treating 'Poisson' as one undifferentiated label.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'Poisson is a discrete family' to 'I can connect process arrivals to Poisson counts with one warrant.'
mission.learning_objective: Describe the Poisson process and the connection between the Poisson process and the Poisson distribution.
mission.concept_focus: Process arrivals → count in an interval → Poisson distribution link; refuse label-collapse.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you evaluated probabilities and quantiles (2.1.3). Today stays on 2.1 at LO 2.1.4 — process connection — using discrete Poisson familiarity from Beta.
mission.why_now: 2.1.4 is the contiguous next LO after evaluation; it bridges counting models to continuous-time arrival stories before generation methods.
mission.expected_benefit: Study Progress for process↔distribution connection — not Topic Complete for 2.1.5–2.1.6.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Gamma Day 2 because syllabus order places process connection after evaluation and before generation.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: process story
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In two to four sentences: what does a Poisson process model, and how does the number of events in a fixed time interval connect to the Poisson distribution?
hints: Count in interval has Poisson distribution under process assumptions.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The LO is the process↔distribution connection, not rote formula dump.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: A Poisson process models random arrivals/events in continuous time at a constant average rate (under standard assumptions). The number of events in a fixed interval then follows a Poisson distribution with mean rate × length.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Only restating the Poisson PMF without the process story.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: refuse label-collapse
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. A student says: 'Poisson just means the discrete distribution — process talk is optional decoration.' Refuse that claim in two sentences with one process↔count warrant.
hints: Process is the continuous-time arrival model.
Distribution is the count law in an interval.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Syllabus 2.1.4 requires the connection, not optional decoration.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse: the Poisson process is the continuous-time arrival model; the Poisson distribution is the law for the count in an interval under that process. Collapsing them loses the LO's required connection.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Agreeing that process language is optional.
